f.title: Apply the binding SÚKL PHV-4 rules to electronic post-authorisation ADR reporting
f.statement: SÚKL guideline PHV-4 is legally binding. It applies to reporting of suspected adverse reactions in the post-authorisation period (reports to the EVPM module of EudraVigilance) and is addressed to marketing authorisation holders and organisations performing E2B(R3) electronic reporting on their behalf. Clinical-trial SUSARs sent to EVCTM follow the EMA and SÚKL Clinical Trials Department guidance instead.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (or organisation reporting on its behalf)
rows.quote: The Guideline concerns the reporting of suspected adverse reactions to medicinal products in their postauthorisation period, i.e. those sent to the EVPM module of the EudraVigilance database. The ADR reports from clinical trials (SUSARs) sent to the EVCTM module of the EudraVigilance database follow the relevant guidances of EMA and the Clinical Trials Department of SÚKL. The Guideline is legally binding.
rows.review_note: National (Czech Republic) SÚKL guideline, legally binding per its text; English version published by SÚKL; marked national. Review: scope row; quote confirms binding status and SUSAR carve-out. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Send ICSRs only as ISO ICH E2B(R3) messages; other formats are non-electronic
f.statement: An electronic report is an individual case safety report in the format defined by ISO ICH E2B(R3), with data items as described by the ICH ICSR M2 guideline and the E2B(R3) Implementation Guide. Reports not meeting this definition (for example sent by e-mail) are treated as non-electronic reports.
f.systems: ICH E2B(R3); ISO ICSR; ICH M2

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (or organisation reporting on its behalf)
rows.quote: An electronic report shall mean an individual case safety report in the format defined by the ISO ICH E2B(R3) guideline, the individual items of which are described by the ICH ICSR M2 guideline and E2B(R3) Implementation Guide. Reports which do not comply with this definition shall be, for the purposes of this guideline, referred to as non-electronic reports, even if they are sent electronically (e.g. by e-mail).
rows.review_note: National (Czech Republic) SÚKL guideline, legally binding per its text; English version published by SÚKL; marked national. Review: binding definition that determines a compliant report. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Treat ICSR submission as complete only when an AA (CA) acknowledgement is received
f.statement: Electronic reporting means transfer of the ichicsr XML message between sender and recipient through EudraVigilance and return of the acknowledgement (ACK). Submission is considered successful and complete only when the sender receives an ACK in the correct format with the value AA - CA.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (or organisation reporting on its behalf)
rows.quote: Electronic report submission is considered successful and completed only if the sender of the message or report receives an ACK in the correct format showing the value of AA – CA.
rows.review_note: National (Czech Republic) SÚKL guideline, legally binding per its text; English version published by SÚKL; marked national. Review: OK. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Submit ICSRs directly to EudraVigilance, not to SÚKL
f.statement: SÚKL does not accept ICSRs from MAHs (since 22 November 2017). MAHs submit their ICSRs directly to EudraVigilance: to ID EVHUMAN for the post-authorisation module (EVPM) and to ID EVCTMPROD for the clinical trial module (EVCTM). SÚKL receives them through EMA re-routing.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (or organisation reporting on its behalf)
rows.quote: At the same time since 22 November 2017 SÚKL has not accepted any ICSRs sent by MAHs, MAHs submit their ICSRs directly to the EV database (to ID EVHUMAN for reports to EVPM module and to ID EVCTMPROD for reports to EVCTM module) within the scope of the centralised reporting.
rows.review_note: National (Czech Republic) SÚKL guideline, legally binding per its text; English version published by SÚKL; marked national. Review: OK. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Retrieve Czech reports received by SÚKL from EudraVigilance
f.statement: SÚKL no longer forwards ADR reports it receives from healthcare professionals or consumers to MAHs; these reports are available to MAHs in EudraVigilance to the extent given by the EV Access Policy.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (or organisation reporting on its behalf)
rows.quote: Since 22 November 2017 SÚKL has not resent any ADR reports received by SÚKL from HCPs or consumers to MAHs. These reports are available for MAHs in EudraVigilance database in the extent given by EV Access Policy.
rows.review_note: National (Czech Republic) SÚKL guideline, legally binding per its text; English version published by SÚKL; marked national. Review: the source states the availability route; the duty to download and process them follows GVP VI. Double-check: actor duty is implied, kept below 90.

f.title: Use the Czech PV contact person as primary contact for ICSR reporting issues
f.statement: Under PHV-6 the MAH must appoint a contact person for pharmacovigilance issues in the Czech Republic. This person ensures communication with SÚKL and is the primary contact for ICSR reporting from the Czech Republic (ICSR data quality issues, technical problems, follow-up requests from SÚKL).
f.processes: Local PV interfaces; Case processing & follow-up

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (or organisation reporting on its behalf)
rows.quote: According to guideline PHV-6 MAH is obliged to appoint a contact person for pharmacovigilance issues in the Czech Republic. Their primary responsibility is to ensure communication with SÚKL, including in the area of ICSR reporting, the contact person for pharmacovigilance issues is the primary contact for issues related to ICSR reporting from the Czech Republic (ICSR data quality issues, technical problems, follow-up requests from SÚKL).
rows.review_note: National (Czech Republic) SÚKL guideline, legally binding per its text; English version published by SÚKL; marked national. Review: OK. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Provide case narrative and reaction text in the reporter's native language for Czech ICSRs
f.statement: For ICSRs from the Czech Republic sent to EudraVigilance, SÚKL requires the case narrative and the reaction/event as reported in the reporter's native language, where available to the MAH, given as verbatim text from the source documents in E2B(R3) fields H.5.r.1a (Case summary and reporter's comments text) and E.i.1.1a (Reaction/event as reported by the primary source in native language).
f.clause: 4.1 Case narrative in reporter's native language
f.applicability: ICSRs originating in the Czech Republic
f.systems: ICH E2B(R3) H.5.r.1a; ICH E2B(R3) E.i.1.1a
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Safety system configuration

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (or organisation reporting on its behalf)
rows.quote: For ICSRs from the Czech Republic sent to the EudraVigilance database it is required by SÚKL to provide information on Case narrative and Reaction/Event as reported in native reporter’s language in case they are available to MAH. Such information should be given in the form of verbatim text according to the report source documents in appropriate E2B (R3) fields (Case Summary and Reporter’s comments Text (H.5.r.1a) and Reaction/Event as reported by the Primary Source in Native Language (E.i.1.1a).
rows.location: 4.1 Case narrative in reporter's native language
rows.review_note: National (Czech Republic) SÚKL guideline, legally binding per its text; English version published by SÚKL; marked national. Review: "it is required" = Mandatory; field placement uses "should". Double-check: OK.

f.title: Add language codes to the native-language narrative and reaction fields
f.statement: Language codes must also be added in E2B(R3) fields H.5.r.1b and E.i.1.1b for the native-language case summary and reaction fields.
f.clause: 4.1 Case narrative in reporter's native language
f.applicability: ICSRs originating in the Czech Republic
f.systems: ICH E2B(R3) H.5.r.1b; ICH E2B(R3) E.i.1.1b
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Safety system configuration

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (or organisation reporting on its behalf)
rows.quote: It is also important to add the language codes to both fields. – in H.5.r.1b and E.i.1.1b fields.
rows.location: 4.1 Case narrative in reporter's native language
rows.review_note: National (Czech Republic) SÚKL guideline, legally binding per its text; English version published by SÚKL; marked national. Review: "it is also important" read as Recommended. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Literature reports: no native-language narrative needed, but native-language reaction text still required
f.statement: The obligation to fill in the native-language case narrative (H.5.r.1a) does not apply to literature reports, since the article is a sufficient description and need not be included or summarised. The obligation to fill in the reaction as reported in the native language (E.i.1.1a) still applies to literature reports.
f.clause: 4.1 Case narrative in reporter's native language
f.exceptions: Native-language narrative not required for literature reports.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (or organisation reporting on its behalf)
rows.quote: The obligation to fill in case narrative in the native language of the reporter (field H.5.r.1a Case Summary and Reporter’s Comments) does not apply to reports from the literature. In this case, a literature article is considered as a sufficient description of the case in the native language; it is not necessary to include it or its summary in the report. The obligation to fill in the reactions as reported by the reporter (field E.i.1.1a Reaction / Event) in the native language of the reporter, however, still applies to reports from the literature.
rows.location: 4.1 Case narrative in reporter's native language
rows.review_note: National (Czech Republic) SÚKL guideline, legally binding per its text; English version published by SÚKL; marked national. Review: OK. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Provide a copy of the source literature article to SÚKL on request
f.statement: SÚKL may ask the MAH that transmitted an initial literature ICSR (occurrence or primary source country Czech Republic) for a copy of the source article. The MAH sends the article, in the format available to it, as an e-mail attachment to the requesting person, with a copy to the SÚKL pharmacovigilance mailbox.
f.applicability: Initial literature ICSRs with occurrence or primary source country Czech Republic

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (or organisation reporting on its behalf)
rows.quote: The article is sent to the person who requested it in the format available to MAH as an e-mail attachment, and in a copy to the address:
rows.review_note: National (Czech Republic) SÚKL guideline, legally binding per its text; English version published by SÚKL; marked national. Review: quote stops before the e-mail address (checker rule); the request context is in the preceding sentence. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Send substantiated follow-up requests to SÚKL only for permitted reasons
f.statement: SÚKL accepts MAH follow-up requests on reports it sent to EudraVigilance only when substantiated; routine follow-up requests are not accepted. Accepted reasons: important additional information needed for case evaluation or reconciliation; clarification of inconsistent ICSR data; further information for signal validation or safety issue evaluation.
f.applicability: Follow-up of ICSRs sent to EudraVigilance by SÚKL
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Local PV interfaces

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (or organisation reporting on its behalf)
rows.quote: Requests have to be always substantiated, SÚKL with reference to the GVP Module VI will not accept routine FU requests.
rows.review_note: National (Czech Republic) SÚKL guideline, legally binding per its text; English version published by SÚKL; marked national. Review: reasons list read in text and summarised. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Include the worldwide case ID, justification and clear questions in follow-up requests to SÚKL
f.statement: A follow-up request to SÚKL (sent by e-mail to the SÚKL pharmacovigilance mailbox) must contain the worldwide unique case identification number, include the justification and be in the form of clearly formulated questions. It must not repeat questions on facts already stated by the reporter; questionnaires are not accepted.
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Local PV interfaces

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (or organisation reporting on its behalf)
rows.quote: The request has to contain worldwide unique case identification number of the report which is going to be followed-up; it has to include the justification for this request; it has to be sent in the form of clearly formulated questions. It must not contain repetitive questions to facts which have already been stated by the reporter in the ICSR. The requests in the form of a questionnaire will also not be accepted.
rows.review_note: National (Czech Republic) SÚKL guideline, legally binding per its text; English version published by SÚKL; marked national. Review: OK. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Follow up own ICSRs when SÚKL asks and submit the follow-up to EudraVigilance
f.statement: SÚKL may ask the MAH, through its Czech PV contact person, to follow up an ICSR the MAH sent to EudraVigilance, in justified cases. The MAH submits the follow-up directly to EudraVigilance; EMA then re-routes it to SÚKL.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder (or organisation reporting on its behalf)
rows.quote: On the other hand, MAH could be asked by SÚKL to follow-up the ICSR which has been sent to EV database by the MAH, in reasonable cases described above. For that purpose, SÚKL will contact MAH’s contact person for pharmacovigilance issues. The elaborated FU is submitted directly to the EV database by the MAH,
rows.review_note: National (Czech Republic) SÚKL guideline, legally binding per its text; English version published by SÚKL; marked national. Review: OK. Double-check: OK.
